tools.name: load_net
tools.description: Load a Petri net (pflow.xyz JSON). Replaces any net with the same name. Nets with guards, stages or rate schedules are refused.

model.description: The net as a JSON object or JSON text

name.description: Name to keep it under; defaults to the model name, else "net"

tools.name: list_nets
tools.description: List loaded nets.

tools.name: state
tools.description: Places, transitions, current marking and enabled transitions. For a pflow.xyz (JSON-LD) net, `info` adds the hosted pflow_info summary: name, colours, each place (initial, capacity, label), transition (rate, label) and arc; its marking and enabled are the initial ones.

net.description: Net name; defaults to the most recently loaded

tools.name: fire
tools.description: Fire one enabled transition and return the new marking. Errors say why it is not enabled.

net.description: Net name; defaults to the most recently loaded

tools.name: reset
tools.description: Return a net to its initial marking.

net.description: Net name; defaults to the most recently loaded

tools.name: simulate
tools.description: Deterministic mass-action ODE (Tsit5) from the current marking. Does not move the marking.

net.description: Net name; defaults to the most recently loaded

contextual.description: How read and inhibitor arcs are treated (default refuse)

tools.name: stochastic
tools.description: Gillespie SSA from the current marking; byte-exact with go-pflow at the same seed. Does not move the marking.

net.description: Net name; defaults to the most recently loaded

tools.name: reachability
tools.description: Explore the reachable markings (pflow-rs reachability, untimed: rates play no part), with parity to pflow.xyz/mcp pflow_reachability: state and edge count, bounded or not, dead markings with the first, transitions that never fire, and three verdicts, each true, false or "unknown": deadlock_free (no reachable marking has nothing enabled, an empty one included), live (L4: from every reachable marking, every transition can still fire) and quasi_live (L1: every transition fires in some reachable marking, which a net with a deadlock can pass). witness is a firing sequence that replays from `from` to the dead marking, or into a closed region shutting transitions out, with never_fires naming them. When complete is false the search stopped at its bound (truncated says why): no verdict is true, and only a witness makes one false. Pass a loaded net by name, or a model inline. Does not move the marking.

net.description: Net name; defaults to the most recently loaded

model.description: A net to analyze without loading it (pflow.xyz JSON object or text); overrides net

max_tokens.description: Tokens in one place past which the net is called unbounded (default 1000)

from.description: Start from the initial marking (default, as the hosted tool) or a loaded net's current one

tools.name: artifact_html
tools.description: Write a self-contained interactive HTML page for a loaded net: click-to-fire token game plus ODE/SSA charts. The pflow WebAssembly engine is embedded, so the page makes no network requests and runs inside a sandboxed artifact. Returns the file path; publish that file as an artifact (the HTML is not returned inline: it is ~250 KB).

net.description: Net name; defaults to the most recently loaded

path.description: Where to write it (default: a temp file)

inline.description: Also return the HTML text. Large; off by default.

tools.name: ontology_describe
tools.description: Look up one term in the bundled pflow ontology: a class, property, glossary concept, pattern or link kind. Give a short name (Place, bounded, pat:queue, lk:event) or a full IRI. Offline: reads the snapshot shipped in this package.

tools.name: ontology_search
tools.description: Find ontology terms whose label, alternative label, name or definition contains the text (case-insensitive). Offline.

tools.name: ontology_classes
tools.description: All classes in the ontology namespace with their direct superclasses, as asserted (a superclass another listed one already implies is left out). Offline.

tools.name: chyp_check
tools.description: Parse and check a Chyp theory (string-diagram rewriting: gens, rules, rewrite proofs). Returns each part with its status and any errors, without diagrams; the theory is kept under a name for chyp_part and chyp_rule.

tools.name: chyp_part
tools.description: One checked part of a kept theory with its diagrams and the proof state after it. Diagram layouts make this large; ask for one part at a time.

tools.name: chyp_rule
tools.description: A named rule of a kept theory: its two sides as diagrams.

tools.name: check
tools.description: Parse a net with go-pflow (the engines' reader) and report its size, colours and anything it refuses. For the editor's full strict check (what normalisation would repair, with paths), open the net in the editor: Check net. Runs locally and offline on pflow-rs (its port of this pflow.xyz/mcp tool, with the same arguments and answer shape); where this says go-pflow, read the pflow-rs port of it.

net.description: A pflow.xyz net (JSON-LD, the editor's format), or the name of a net loaded with load_net; defaults to the most recently loaded

tools.name: cid
tools.description: The CID a net seals to: URDNA2015 canonical N-Quads, sha256, CIDv1 base58btc. The same as /api/save, the editor and pflow-native (top-level @id ignored). Runs locally and offline on pflow-rs (its port of this pflow.xyz/mcp tool, with the same arguments and answer shape); where this says go-pflow, read the pflow-rs port of it.

net.description: A pflow.xyz net (JSON-LD, the editor's format), or the name of a net loaded with load_net; defaults to the most recently loaded

tools.name: edit
tools.description: Build or edit a net. Give `net` (omit it to start from an empty net) and an ordered list of `ops`; all are applied or none (an error names the failing op). Returns the changed net, its CID and a size summary. Stores nothing: pass the returned net back in for the next edit, or to pflow.xyz/mcp pflow_save. Ops (each {op, ...}): add_place{id?,label?,initial?,capacity?,x?,y?}, add_transition{id?,label?,rate?,x?,y?}, add_arc{source,target,weight?,inhibit?}, set_arc{source,target,weight?,inhibit?}, delete_arc{source,target}, set_place{id,initial?,capacity?} (capacity 0/null = unbounded), add_tokens{id,delta?,color?}, set_rate{id,rate}, set_label{id,label}, rename{id,new_id}, move{id,x,y}, delete{ids}, set_details{name?,description?}. Ids default to p0,p1,… / t0,t1,…; x,y default to a tidy grid. An arc joins a place and a transition; inhibit on place→transition is an inhibitor arc, on transition→place a read arc. Runs locally and offline on pflow-rs (its port of this pflow.xyz/mcp tool, with the same arguments and answer shape); where this says go-pflow, read the pflow-rs port of it.

net.description: A pflow.xyz net (JSON-LD, the editor's format), or the name of a net loaded with load_net; defaults to the most recently loaded

tools.name: info
tools.description: Summarise a net: name, colours, every place (initial, capacity), transition (rate) and arc, plus the current marking and which transitions are enabled in it. Runs locally and offline on pflow-rs (its port of this pflow.xyz/mcp tool, with the same arguments and answer shape); where this says go-pflow, read the pflow-rs port of it.

net.description: A pflow.xyz net (JSON-LD, the editor's format), or the name of a net loaded with load_net; defaults to the most recently loaded

tools.name: validate
tools.description: go-pflow's structural checks: structure, connectivity, deadlocks, unboundedness, conservation (with the net's conservation laws as equations). With reachability=true also explores the state space (bounded by max_states). Errors and warnings carry the affected nodes and a suggestion. Runs locally and offline on pflow-rs (its port of this pflow.xyz/mcp tool, with the same arguments and answer shape); where this says go-pflow, read the pflow-rs port of it.

net.description: A pflow.xyz net (JSON-LD, the editor's format), or the name of a net loaded with load_net; defaults to the most recently loaded

tools.name: verify
tools.description: Check properties of a net and get proved / refuted / unknown with evidence: a structural proof from an invariant, or a replayable firing sequence for a counterexample (go-pflow verify). `properties` is a list of {kind, ...}: deadlock-free (a marking that drained to empty counts as finished), bounded, live (L1: every transition fires in some reachable marking, which a net with a deadlock can pass), l4-live (from every reachable marking, every transition can still fire), terminating, conserves, reachable{target:{place:n}}, unreachable{target}, invariant{expr:"a + b == 3"}, mutual-exclusion{places:[…],bound}. A reachable verdict carries the firing sequence. Unknown means the search hit max_states, not a pass. Runs locally and offline on pflow-rs (its port of this pflow.xyz/mcp tool, with the same arguments and answer shape); where this says go-pflow, read the pflow-rs port of it.

net.description: A pflow.xyz net (JSON-LD, the editor's format), or the name of a net loaded with load_net; defaults to the most recently loaded

tools.name: invariants
tools.description: Minimal semi-positive P-invariants (conservation laws, valued at the net's marking) and T-invariants (firing multisets that return the net to its marking), by Farkas elimination on the incidence matrix. `kind` is p, t or both (default both). `truncated` is true if the elimination hit its row limit: what is listed is valid, but may be incomplete. Runs locally and offline on pflow-rs (its port of this pflow.xyz/mcp tool, with the same arguments and answer shape); where this says go-pflow, read the pflow-rs port of it.

net.description: A pflow.xyz net (JSON-LD, the editor's format), or the name of a net loaded with load_net; defaults to the most recently loaded

tools.name: incidence
tools.description: The incidence matrix C = post − pre (rows: places, columns: transitions, both sorted by id; inhibitor and read arcs move nothing and are left out). Runs locally and offline on pflow-rs (its port of this pflow.xyz/mcp tool, with the same arguments and answer shape); where this says go-pflow, read the pflow-rs port of it.

net.description: A pflow.xyz net (JSON-LD, the editor's format), or the name of a net loaded with load_net; defaults to the most recently loaded

tools.name: export
tools.description: The net as `json` (normalised pflow.xyz JSON-LD with its CID, the default) or `svg` (the server's drawing of it; `layout` may be force-atlas-2, circular or hierarchical). Runs locally and offline on pflow-rs (its port of this pflow.xyz/mcp tool, with the same arguments and answer shape); where this says go-pflow, read the pflow-rs port of it.

net.description: A pflow.xyz net (JSON-LD, the editor's format), or the name of a net loaded with load_net; defaults to the most recently loaded

tools.name: sde
tools.description: Chemical Langevin SDE (Euler-Maruyama over the mass-action propensities, 20 steps per sample interval; go-pflow's portable path, seeded) from the net's marking with each transition's rate: continuous state with the net's own firing noise, cheap at large token counts where SSA is slow. With runs > 1 the series are means with a ± std-dev band. The same numbers as pflow-native's sim.sde for the same seed (and the editor's, on a net that lists its transitions in id order). Refuses a net with inhibitor or read arcs, or a capacity on a place some firing adds tokens to, which a diffusion cannot express (use pflow.xyz/mcp pflow_ssa). A value that overflows is null, as native writes it. The answer always fits whole: with the default points the server returns as many of the 101 as fit (and says so in `note`); asking for more points than fit is refused, naming how many do. `places` returns fewer series. Runs locally and offline on pflow-rs (its port of this pflow.xyz/mcp tool, with the same arguments and answer shape); where this says go-pflow, read the pflow-rs port of it.

dt.description: integration step (default (t_end / (points-1)) / 20); the run then takes t_end / (20 dt) sample intervals, thinned to points

net.description: A pflow.xyz net (JSON-LD, the editor's format), or the name of a net loaded with load_net; defaults to the most recently loaded

places.description: places whose series to return (default all; a document place selects all its colours); finals always cover every place

points.description: points returned, 0 to t_end (default 101, fewer when that many would not fit the answer; ≤ 500)

seed.description: RNG seed (default 1, at most 2^53); realization r uses seed + r

tools.name: what_if
tools.description: What if `place` had `delta` more tokens (default 1; negative removes)? Runs the net as is and with the change on go-pflow's scenario SSA (the discrete engine: inhibitors, read arcs and capacities respected), both arms on one shared seed so the difference measures the change, not the dice. Returns each arm's summary (final means and spread, time-weighted mean and p95, throughput, depletion, contention), an overlay time series (group = arm), a table of final means, and each arm's finals table (mean, sd, min, max). The editor's sim.what_if; the same numbers as pflow-native for the same seed. The answer always fits whole: with the default samples the server returns as many of the 60 as fit (and says so in `note`); asking for more samples than fit is refused, naming how many do. `places` returns fewer series; every place stays in the summaries and finals. Runs locally and offline on pflow-rs (its port of this pflow.xyz/mcp tool, with the same arguments and answer shape); where this says go-pflow, read the pflow-rs port of it.

delta.description: tokens to add (default 1; may be negative)

net.description: A pflow.xyz net (JSON-LD, the editor's format), or the name of a net loaded with load_net; defaults to the most recently loaded

places.description: places whose series to return (default all; a document place selects all its colours); finals always cover every place

samples.description: sample points, 0 to t_end (default 60, fewer when that many would not fit the answer; ≤ 500)

tools.name: bundle_example
tools.description: The catalog of parts to snap together and a composition of them to start from: a PetriNetBundle of pattern instances (orders, a bounded queue; workers, a resource pool; payment, a two-step saga with compensation; and the extras payment2, orders2, workers2), built by go-pflow's constructors, joined by the three idioms (an event link each from orders' dequeue to workers' acquire and payment's do:reserve, and from workers' release to payment's commit) or by `links` you give. `instances` picks from the catalog (default orders, workers, payment); a link whose end is not in the composition is dropped and listed; a link Validate refuses fails the call, as bundle_add_link would. Returns `bundle` (pass it to the other pflow.xyz/mcp pflow_bundle_* tools), the `catalog` with the parameters and the reason for each, and the four `scenarios` (scripts for bundle_run with the predicates they expect: commit, refund, charge-fails, second-order). The same catalog, parameters and scenarios as the composition page (pflow.xyz/compose.html). Runs locally and offline on pflow-rs (its port of this pflow.xyz/mcp tool, with the same arguments and answer shape); where this says go-pflow, read the pflow-rs port of it.

instances.description: catalog instance ids (default orders, workers, payment)

tools.name: bundle_validate
tools.description: Check a composition (go-pflow's Bundle.Validate): subnets (unique ids, models, ports on exported places, arc types), then every link (endpoints exist, the kind fits the ends, the net types allow it, port schemas agree, token-link direction, a data link's observer moves nothing, guard conditions). Returns valid, errors and warnings, each {code, message, element}. Errors name the link as links[i] (or its id). Warnings do not block flattening: an untyped subnet, an unbounded queue, a workflow net without exactly one token, a guard link restricting its subnet. Runs locally and offline on pflow-rs (its port of this pflow.xyz/mcp tool, with the same arguments and answer shape); where this says go-pflow, read the pflow-rs port of it.

bundle.description: a composition, a PetriNetBundle: {"@type": "PetriNetBundle", "name", "subnets": [{"id", "net_type" (ResourceNet, WorkflowNet, GameNet, ComputationNet, ClassificationNet or omitted), "model": {"places": [{"id", "initial", "exported", "capacity", "kind": "token"|"data"}], "transitions": [{"id"}], "arcs": [{"from", "to", "weight", "type": "read"|"inhibitor"}], "constraints": [{"id", "expr"}]}, "ports": [{"id", "kind": "in"|"out"|"inout"|"observe", "place"|("target": "transition", "transition"), "schema"}]}], "links": [{"kind": "token"|"data"|"event"|"guard", "from": {"subnet", "port"}, "to": {"subnet", "port"}, "id", "condition"}], "namespace", "arc_merge": "sum"|"max"}. pflow_bundle_example returns one to start from. Limits: names (ids) of at most 128 bytes, counts and weights below 2^53, at most 32 subnets, 1000 places, 1000 transitions, 4000 arcs, 512 ports, 200 links and 200 constraints. Give every arc an explicit weight: one with none fires as 1 but counts as 0 in the incidence matrix (and, for a lone subnet, in the flat arcs). A subnet that declares no ports has one per exported place, named for it (pflow_bundle_candidates alone does not derive them); a port on a transition has to be declared. A link in the document may also name {subnet, place} or {subnet, transition} for an end that has no port. Fields not named here are ignored without a word (`tokens` on a place does nothing, it is `initial`; `inhibit: true` on an arc does nothing, it is `type: "inhibitor"`); a misspelt net_type, place kind, port kind or target, link kind or arc_merge is refused. A bundle and the flat net it makes are not pflow.xyz nets: pflow_simulate, pflow_fire and the other net tools cannot read them.

tools.name: bundle_add_link
tools.description: Snap two parts together by adding a link to a composition: judge it as Validate does on the two subnets it joins and the page's two rules (a link joins two different subnets; the same link is not added twice, an event link either way round), and if legal return the composition's links with it appended. A refused link is an error (isError) listing each reason as "[CODE] message", and for a port that is not there the ports its subnet has. Ends are ports: "subnet:port" or {subnet, port} (a subnet that declares no ports has one per exported place; to link a transition, declare a port for it in the bundle). Returns the new link's index, key, verdict (ok, errors, warnings: a guard link warns that it restricts) and `links`. It takes kind, from and to only: a link's id, a guard link's condition and its lowering cannot be set here, add them to the returned link before passing the links back in the bundle. Stores nothing. Runs locally and offline on pflow-rs (its port of this pflow.xyz/mcp tool, with the same arguments and answer shape); where this says go-pflow, read the pflow-rs port of it.

from.description: the link's from end (an event link either way round; a guard's from is the gated transition): "subnet:port" or {subnet, port}

to.description: the link's to end (a guard's to is the observed place): "subnet:port" or {subnet, port}

tools.name: bundle_candidates
tools.description: The snap-together candidates: every other port of the composition, judged as the far end of a link dragged from `from`. Kinds are tried in order (transition to transition: event; transition to place: guard; place to transition: a guard oriented transition to place; place to place: token, then data) and the first legal one wins; `prefer` restricts to one kind. Returns `lit` (how many are legal) and for each port its ref, key, ok, the link it would make, its verdict and each kind tried, in the order of the bundle's subnets and ports; `only_ok` returns just the legal ones (otherwise every other port is listed, those of the same subnet among them, which are never legal (PAGE_SAME_SUBNET), and a long answer is cut by the result limit). A port the link would repeat is not legal either (PAGE_DUPLICATE). Only declared ports count here, both `from` and the candidates: a subnet with no "ports" array offers none (the other tools derive one port per exported place); a refused `from` names the ports its subnet has. Runs locally and offline on pflow-rs (its port of this pflow.xyz/mcp tool, with the same arguments and answer shape); where this says go-pflow, read the pflow-rs port of it.

tools.name: bundle_flatten
tools.description: Flatten a composition into one net (go-pflow's Bundle.FlattenWithMap): token and data links fuse places (named wire:<canonical member>), event links fuse transitions (named by the link's id, else fused:<members>), a guard link lowers to a read or inhibitor arc; elements are prefixed <subnet>/ unless the bundle sets namespace false. Returns the flat places, transitions (each with the members it came from), arcs and constraints, the wires and fused groups, the place and transition maps (subnet to local id to flat id), the warnings and each transition's enablement at the initial marking with go-pflow's reason. A bundle Validate refuses answers {ok: false, error}, not an error of the call; a flat net whose answer would pass about 2 MB (a fused name is repeated everywhere it is mentioned) is an error of the call. The flat net is not a pflow.xyz net: simulate, fire and the other net tools cannot read it, bundle_run fires it. Give every arc an explicit weight: an arc with none fires as 1, but a lone subnet is returned as written, with weight 0 (a `notes` entry says how many). Two event links that share an id and fuse different transitions merge into one flat transition (the last class by smallest member names its fused group and description). Runs locally and offline on pflow-rs (its port of this pflow.xyz/mcp tool, with the same arguments and answer shape); where this says go-pflow, read the pflow-rs port of it.

tools.name: bundle_run
tools.description: Fire a script on the flat net from its initial marking (go-pflow's firing rule, weights, read and inhibitor arcs, capacities): `script` is a list of members "<subnet>/<transition>", the transition's own id in its subnet (payment/do_charge, not the port id do:charge a link names; a member of a fused transition fires the whole fusion), or `scenario` one of the example's four. Stops at the first member that is not in the net or cannot fire and says why, then evaluates the predicates. `expect` (with `script`) is a list of {place, n, says}: the place, as "<subnet>/<place>", must hold n tokens at the end. Returns the steps (member, the flat transition it fired, enabled, why not), whether the script completed, the final marking and each predicate's actual and pass. A negative arc weight never enables (as in pflow-rs), counts saturate at the ends of int64, an arc with no weight fires as 1. The flat net is not a pflow.xyz net; this is how to fire it. Runs locally and offline on pflow-rs (its port of this pflow.xyz/mcp tool, with the same arguments and answer shape); where this says go-pflow, read the pflow-rs port of it.

bundle.description: a composition, a PetriNetBundle: {"@type": "PetriNetBundle", "name", "subnets": [{"id", "net_type" (ResourceNet, WorkflowNet, GameNet, ComputationNet, ClassificationNet or omitted), "model": {"places": [{"id", "initial", "exported", "capacity", "kind": "token"|"data"}], "transitions": [{"id"}], "arcs": [{"from", "to", "weight", "type": "read"|"inhibitor"}], "constraints": [{"id", "expr"}]}, "ports": [{"id", "kind": "in"|"out"|"inout"|"observe", "place"|("target": "transition", "transition"), "schema"}]}], "links": [{"kind": "token"|"data"|"event"|"guard", "from": {"subnet", "port"}, "to": {"subnet", "port"}, "id", "condition"}], "namespace", "arc_merge": "sum"|"max"}. pflow_bundle_example returns one to start from. Limits: names (ids) of at most 128 bytes, counts and weights below 2^53, at most 32 subnets, 1000 places, 1000 transitions, 4000 arcs, 512 ports, 200 links and 200 constraints. Give every arc an explicit weight: one with none fires as 1 but counts as 0 in the incidence matrix (and, for a lone subnet, in the flat arcs). A subnet that declares no ports has one per exported place, named for it (pflow_bundle_candidates alone does not derive them); a port on a transition has to be declared. A link in the document may also name {subnet, place} or {subnet, transition} for an end that has no port. Fields not named here are ignored without a word (`tokens` on a place does nothing, it is `initial`; `inhibit: true` on an arc does nothing, it is `type: "inhibitor"`); a misspelt net_type, place kind, port kind or target, link kind or arc_merge is refused. A bundle and the flat net it makes are not pflow.xyz nets: pflow_simulate, pflow_fire and the other net tools cannot read them.

expect.description: predicates on the final marking (with script)

scenario.description: instead of a script: one of the example's scenarios (its script and predicates; it names the example's members, so on another composition it stops at the first)

tools.name: bundle_incidence
tools.description: The flat net's incidence matrix C = post − pre (rows: flat places, columns: flat transitions, in the flat net's order; read and inhibitor arcs move nothing), each subnet's own block, and each declared constraint of the form tokens("a") + … == n read as a P-invariant y (1 on each place it names): holds is true when y·C = 0 and y·M₀ = n, which proves the constraint for every reachable marking, false when it does not, and null when the constraint is not such a sum. A bundle Validate refuses answers {ok: false, error}; matrices of more than 50000 cells in all (flat places x flat transitions, plus each subnet's own) are an error of the call. Give every arc an explicit weight: an arc with none counts as 0 in a subnet's own block (and everywhere for a lone subnet) but fires as 1, so that column is wrong (a `notes` entry says how many arcs; pflow-native's matrix does the same). The flat net is not a pflow.xyz net. Runs locally and offline on pflow-rs (its port of this pflow.xyz/mcp tool, with the same arguments and answer shape); where this says go-pflow, read the pflow-rs port of it.
